verses.1: And it happened that when Jesus had finished speaking all these words, he said to his disciples:
verses.2: You know that after two days, the Passover festival begins. And the son of man is handed over for crucifixion.
verses.3: Then the high priests and the elders of the people gathered in the temple of the high priest called Caiaphas.
verses.4: And they conspired to keep Jesus captive and kill him.
verses.5: They said, “It should not be done during the festival, so that no noise is created among the people.”
verses.6: And when Jesus was born in Bethlehem, in the house of Simon the Levite,
verses.7: A woman came to him, carrying a garland of extremely expensive beads. She placed it on his head in a inverted position.
verses.8: But seeing this, the disciples became angry and said, “What kind of loss is this?”
verses.9: For this could be done by many people, and given to the poor.
verses.10: But Jesus said to them, “What do you give in exchange for this woman?” For she had done a good work for me.
verses.11: For always do you have the poor with you, but I never have them with me.
verses.12: For by placing this needle on my body, it became possible for me to be born again.
verses.13: I say to you, if this message of salvation is proclaimed throughout the world, then it will also be known what he did for his own memory.
verses.14: Then, one of the twelve men, called Judas Iscariot, went before the high priests.
verses.15: He said, “What do you want me to give you? They offered him thirty silver coins.”
verses.16: And from that time on, he sought an opportunity to get rid of him.
verses.17: And when they arrived at the first altar, the disciples came to Jesus and said, “What do you want me to prepare for your feast?”
verses.18: And he said, “Go into the city and speak to him.” The teacher replied, “My time is limited. I will spend my fasting with my students.”
verses.19: And the disciples prepared as Jesus had commanded them, and they set aside the day for fasting.
verses.20: However, the Opsiaship was achieved after those twelve students.
verses.21: And when they were about to give them up, he said, “I tell you that one of you will be able to deliver me.”
verses.22: And they began to say to him, “With deep sorrow, each one of them said to him: ‘Am I, Lord, not worthy to have you stay with me?’”
verses.23: But the one who replied said, “You have placed my hand in that box with you. You will be the one to deliver me there.”
verses.24: The son of man is who brings about what is written about him. But it’s not the man himself who gives birth to that son. It would be good for him if he hadn’t been born from that man at all.
verses.25: Then Judas, who had betrayed him, said to him, “Am I not, oh Rabbi?” He replied, “You said so.”
verses.26: After taking some bread from them, Jesus blessed it and said to his disciples, “Take and eat. This is my body.”
verses.27: And taking a cup and expressing his thanks, he gave them it, saying, “Drink from it all.”
verses.28: This is therefore the “firmament” of my covenant—the part that is stretched out to cover away many sins.
verses.29: I tell you, do not drink this wine until the day after that day comes. When I drink it with you, it’s a new thing in my father’s kingdom.
verses.30: And after praying, we went up to the Mountain of Oil.
verses.31: Then Jesus said to them, “All of you will be scattered among me in this same night. It is written, ‘I will raise up a shepherd for my sheep.’ Then the sheep of the flock will be scattered.”
verses.32: After this uprising, I will lead you into Galilee.
verses.33: Then Peter replied to him, “If all people are going to be thrown into hell, then I certainly won’t be thrown into hell either.”
verses.34: Jesus said to him, “I tell you that in this same night, before the cock crow, three people will deny him.”
verses.35: Peter said to him, “Even if I must die along with you, I will not refuse your request.” Similarly, all the disciples also said the same thing.
verses.36: Then Jesus comes along with them to a place called Gethsemane. He says to his disciples, “Sit here until I go away there.”
verses.37: And after taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedaeus, he began to grieve and to be upset.
verses.38: Then he says to them, “My soul is in torment until death. Please stay with me and help me through this time.”
verses.39: And as he stepped forward, he fell to his knees in front of him, praying and saying, “Father, if it is possible, please take away this cup from me. But not as I wish, but as You wish.”
verses.40: And he came to his disciples and found them being distracted. He said to Peter, “Surely you cannot keep up with me for one hour?”
verses.41: Hurry up and pray, so that you may not fall into temptation. The spirit is ready, but the body is weak.
verses.42: Once again, after leaving the second place, he said, “Father, if it isn’t possible for this to happen without his permission, then let your will be done.”
verses.43: And when they came back again, they found them still trying to see. After all, their eyes were swollen from the pain.
verses.44: And after they left again, he began to speak again from the third person.
verses.45: Then he comes to his disciples and says to them, “Rest a little while. See, the hour has come; and the Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of sinners.”
verses.46: arise, let us go; see, the traitor is about to deliver me.
verses.47: And while he was still speaking, I saw Judas coming along with one of the twelve. Along with him was a large crowd, armed with swords and sticks, members of the priests and elders of the people.
verses.48: But the one who handed him over gave them a sign, saying, “This is the one I am going to kiss. Keep him safe.”
verses.49: And as soon as he came near Jesus, he said, “Thank you, Rabbi.” And he welcomed him.
verses.50: But Jesus said to them, “Take away the stones from here.” Then they went and laid their hands on Jesus’s shoulders and believed in him.
verses.51: And one of those who were with Jesus saw that he took off his sword. Then he seized the slave of the high priest and freed him from his bonds.
verses.52: Then Jesus said to him, “Put away your sword; for all who take up a sword will be killed.” For those who take up swords in battle, they will surely die.
verses.53: Do you think that I cannot ask my father for help? Would it be better for him to give me twelve more messages instead?
verses.54: How, then, can the writings be considered valid if it must happen in such a way?
verses.55: In that hour, Jesus said to the crowd, “How often do you go into the wilderness with sticks and stones to gather wood? Every day, in the temple, I teach, yet you do not listen to me.”
verses.56: All of this happened so that the prophecies of the prophets could be fulfilled. At that time, all the disciples abandoned him and ran away.
verses.57: Those who kept Jesus took him to Caiaphas, the high priest. There, the officials and elders gathered together.
verses.58: And Peter followed him from afar until he reached the palace of the high priest. Once inside, he sat down among the servants, hoping to see the end of this whole situation.
verses.59: But the high priests and the entire council sought to bring false charges against Jesus, in order to kill him.
verses.60: And not many false witnesses came forward. Later on, two more came forward.
verses.61: They said, “He said, ‘I can build the temple of God in three days.’”
verses.62: And the high priest said to him, “Do not say anything. What do these people have to accuse you?”
verses.63: But Jesus remained silent. Then the high priest said to him, “I condemn you to God alive, so that you may say for us whether you are indeed the Son of God.”
verses.64: Jesus said to him, “You have said that I will do more than what I have already done for you. From now on, you shall see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of God and coming on the clouds of heaven.”
verses.65: Then the high priest ripped off his clothes, saying, “What need do we still have for witnesses? Now, hear this insult.”
verses.66: What do you think? Those who answered said, “It’s a death due to guilt.”
verses.67: Then they planted them on his face and covered him with them. They also decorated him accordingly.
verses.68: Saying, “Prophecy for us, Christ! Who is the one who has deceived you?”
verses.69: And Peter sat outside in the courtyard. Then a little girl came up to him and said, “You will also be with Jesus of Galilee.”
verses.70: But he refused to say anything in front of everyone. “I don’t know what you’re saying.”
verses.71: When he went out to the gate, he saw another man there, and he said to those who were there, “This man was with Jesus of Nazareth.”
verses.72: And once again, he denied it after taking an oath, saying that he didn’t know that person at all.
verses.73: After going a little further, the elders said to Peter, “Truly, you too are one of them. For your speech clearly shows that you belong to them.”
verses.74: Then he began to complain and say that he didn’t know that person at all. And immediately, he cried out in anger.
verses.75: And Peter remembered the words that Jesus had said: “Three times I will call upon your name.” When he heard this, he became angry and rushed out of the room.
